utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Davidovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we begin, I wished to put this on record. On Friday last week, the Chamber issued a redaction order of a portion of the public audio-visual record of the hearing so as to delete a conversation which was unrelated to these proceedings and which could be heard on the French channel. Thank you. Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Davidovic. On Friday, we stopped after having played a part of a video showing an award ceremony in Kula, and we had seen the man, Zika Crnogorac reporting to Jovica Stanisic. Although we couldn't hear the words spoken in the English at that time, I don't see a reason to repeat this. I would ask that the video be played, 65 ter 45235; however, another section. And the section to be played is at 00:09:02. And as we are seeing it, Mr. Davidovic, would you please tell us whom you recognise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I recognise Mr. Milosevic and Jovica Stanisic, and this is Zika Crnogorac; Zika, nicknamed Crnogorac.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can stop here. That is at 00:00:34. Can we now please move on to number 00:15:36, and we will hear something said.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And my first question to you would be, if you hear it: Who is speaking? And then we will listen to what is being said.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: If you recognise someone, please.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vucevic; Milosevic; Jovica Stanisic; Petar Gracanin, my minister; Mr. Kertes. Frenki is the person who is speaking, but let me see a few more faces.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Would you please concentrate now on the text also, what is said? Mr. Davidovic, having heard what was said, does that confirm your own observations in relation to where this group was actually deployed in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this refers to all the places where that unit had fought.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to have this video admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have a transcript for this?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It was actually -- yes, we do have a transcript for this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, because it was not read out and it's not reflected in the transcript, so that it's better if we have that separate transcribed script. Could you give the number? Is it in the same number?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's the same number, Your Honours. It's a transcript in both languages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have the entire clip or do we have a separate number for this clip?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would actually ask to have the entire clip be admitted. But if you prefer differently --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The entire clip, in terms of length, how long would it be?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's quite a lengthy -- a lengthy -- but it's mostly people attending the award. It's 48 minutes, I'm just told, 48 minutes. Part of this is the speech, part of what we heard, and a lot of this is basically people being greeted and these kind of things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the clarity, I'm minded to admit those parts that we saw in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's fine. Yes, that's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted. I don't think there's any objection to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. We preferred the way you've decided to do it also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll give it an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2852, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would also include, of course, the Friday clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. I would ask that as the next exhibit, P01105 be called up. And as it is coming up: It's a transcript from the 22nd RS Assembly session of the 23rd and the 24th of November, 1992. And we would need on the screen the English, page 20, the top part, and the B/C/S version, page 18, the bottom part. Page 18. Just for Mr. Davidovic, you see who's speaking here at the Assembly session. Can we please have in the B/C/S now the next page?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, Ms. Plavsic, as a response to Mico Stanisic, is stating here the following. She says that: "It is the truth, not rumours, Minister, that after the statement by the president of the republic, that is, his call to volunteers in all Serbian lands and other Orthodox countries, I sent letters to all addresses. My intention was to collect anybody who was willing to fight for the Serbian cause ..." And she also refers to letters being sent to Seselj, to Arkan, and to Jovic. Mr. Davidovic, are you aware of this Assembly session, and did you have -- did you review this part during your preparation for the testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had heard earlier on that there was a debate at the Assembly session concerning volunteers, and I heard that Biljana had clearly said that she was the one who had called upon these volunteers to come, and in writing, at that. And I had an opportunity of seeing this document during my first proofing with the Prosecutor. That was the first time I saw this.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And do you know whether the president of the Republika Srpska, that is, Mr. Karadzic, called for volunteers?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I also heard that Mr. Karadzic had asked that all of those who wished to fight for Republika Srpska should report as volunteers and come to Bosnia, join the units of the army, and fight on the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have a reference for this?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could only the speaker's microphone be on, please. We can barely hear the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Here is also mentioned Mr. Jovic, who was sent a letter. Who would that be, if you know him, and do you know whether certain paramilitaries or volunteers were associated with him?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that Mr. Jovic is from Pazova, either Stari Pazova or Nova Pazova. I think they were called the Eagles, or the Falcons, or something like that. They were also volunteers in the territory of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, would you be minded to take up the objections of Mr. Karadzic, in terms of when and where did he hear that? I'll ask him. Mr. Davidovic, you said you heard that Mr. Karadzic had asked the volunteers to come to Bosnia, but can you help us, in terms of when and where did you hear and when and where did he speak about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard that several times, not only from one person, but several persons. I heard it from military personnel, from members of the authorities, too. If I were to remember individually who it was, I was also informed about this from Mico Stanisic, and his assistants, his associates, and military personnel who were there at the time; Colonel Ilic, commander of the corps. And I had a great many other conversations with people. This was, more or less, a generally-known thing. It wasn't some kind of a secret or it's not something that was being concealed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document is already in evidence. There's no need to admit it. I would ask that Exhibit 65 ter 07347 be brought up on the screen, please. And as it is coming up: It is a report of the chief of the CSB Bijeljina, Mr. Jesuric, to the RS MUP, of the 21st of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, Mr. Jesuric is referring here to the security situation and to the behaviour of certain informal and uncontrolled paramilitary groups, which he calls soldiers from the front, and the problems they caused in relation to crime prevention. Mr. Davidovic, were you aware that these problems existed in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, such things did happen in the area of Bijeljina, Zvornik, Brcko; that is, that area that is covered by the CSB Bijeljina. And that is what Predrag Jesuric is speaking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would request the admission of this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2853, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would now ask that video-clip 65 ter 45359A be played, and just the sequence 00:34:30 to 00:36:26. And if you would tell us whom you see, and then, of course, listen to what is said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Arkan; Zeljko Raznatovic, nicknamed Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can see what is written there. I don't know whether this can be read into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure the accused can hear the B/C/S. We have sound, don't we?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We should have sound. I'm also surprised that nothing is coming. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What can be done about it, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: A technician is coming to take a look.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Perhaps we can wait until this is done and go on with something else in between.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. But, actually, we do have another -- we do have another video-clip, and I hope that this works now. It's 65 ter 45048, and I would request to play the parts 00:01:00 to 00:04:05. It is in Sanction with subtitles, but it should also be audible.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I see it's not working either, so we can see how this can be fixed. We can move on. Your Honour, it will take a minute.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's not functioning. We have to do this in the break, and we can move on using now documents. Can I please have 65 ter 13290 be brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Davidovic, it is a document which purports to be a letter from the Party for Serbian Unity to the president of Republika Srpska, dated the 16th of April, 1994. Mr. Davidovic, did you have an opportunity to see this document in the preparation for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it in the OTP during my proofing.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know the Party for Serbian Unity and his [sic] leader?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Party for Serbian Unity is a party that was founded by Zeljko Raznatovic, Arkan, who led the party and who had a certain number of supporters. I think that he actually had four or five -- or, actually, six seats in the Serbian Parliament. This is a document I looked at earlier on, and I think that it primarily refers to the telegram of support that was sent when the NATO bombing took place. They are being supported here to continue with their heroic resistance. And, if necessary, he is expecting a call to join the armed forces, which can be seen unequivocally from this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Davidovic, looking at the address of this party, do you know this address?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the street where Mr. Arkan's house is to this day; the late Arkan, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would request the admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2854, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we now please have item 65 ter 01596 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, in many paragraphs in your statement, you refer to problems with paramilitary formations, and we do not need to repeat this here. And as this is now on the screen, it is a report on paramilitary formations in the territory of the Republika Srpska, issued by the VRS Main Staff on the 28th of July, 1992. In your written statement, you, indeed, refer to this report. And, Your Honour, that's at paragraph 77. Did you review this report when you came to The Hague to prepare for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I reviewed this document in the OTP, and even before I came here I knew that the military security had compiled an analysis about the situation among the military units that was submitted to the Main Staff. On the basis of this assessment that was written up by Tolimir, an order followed which was written by Radovan Karadzic, in which he asks for urgent measures to be taken throughout Republika Srpska and measures that would be aimed at removing the paramilitaries or placing them under the command of the Army of Republika Srpska. This document reflects the situation as it actually was, the real situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And as the paramilitaries -- the groups described here on the first page and their behaviour, would that be correct, a correct assessment?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can we have the second page, please, in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, in the complex paragraph in the middle on that page, reference is made to the fact that such groups hiding behind official authorities, behind the ruling party. Did you, yourself, make observation to this effect?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what? It is hard to explain and hard to say these are volunteers of a political party. Usually they come in groups, bigger or smaller ones. They introduce themselves as being representatives or members of some political party, and then they report in the Army of Republika Srpska. Now, whether they're actually members of that political party or not, it is hard to say. Later on, it would turn out very quickly that they didn't belong to anyone, that they were self-organised, that quite a few of these people had come to the front-line with criminal intent, just to loot. I'm not sure that they were under any political party. Perhaps they were sympathisers or supporters, but that is totally insignificant in relation to what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have page 5 in the English, and the focus would be on the middle of the page, and page 5 in the B/C/S, more to the bottom, focusing in the B/C/S more to the bottom. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You see here a paragraph with this reference to Mauzer and the Serbian National Guard, and their backing by the Bijeljina SDS. Is that a correct assessment that is provided here?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I'm going to try to explain. At the start of the war, it was believed that the army, the former JNA, should not be defending the Serbian people because they considered it to be a traitorist army, a former Communist army, and that this was something that was to be left behind. And they felt that they should form a military formation that should be exclusively under the control of the SDS, and that is why the crisis staffs in the municipalities of Bijeljina and Zvornik, and, more or less, everywhere, as far as I know, formed different units. In Bijeljina, this was the Serbian National Guard. In Ugljevik, it was an independent unit under the TO Staff, but it was commanded from the beginning by Mitar, Mando was his nickname. So wherever I had the opportunity to go, I encountered these units which were exclusively under the command of the Crisis Staff or the SDS. I even have an explanation of why they were doing that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, just one clarification. The Serbian National Guard in Bijeljina, who was their head, the commander of them?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Ljubisa Savic, aka Mauzer.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This Mando that you just mentioned, that is the group referred to in the next paragraph; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a group that was formed by the SDS TO Staff, headed by a person called Mando.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the persons mentioned in that paragraph, the last sentence, these people, do you know them and to which bodies they belong?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of them, and I know under whose command they were. I even knew some individuals who were members of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to have this document admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2855, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm also informed that the videos are now working, and I would like to try this again. Can we please have now 65 ter 45359A and play it. And as I said, it's from 00:34:30 to 00:36:26.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: My information was incorrect. Thank you. We continue, then, with documents. Your Honour, we continue with a video. However, there is no spoken text on it, so I think that allows us to play it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think I found the transcript in both languages, B/C/S and English. If Defence is fine, we can move on. But that's the problem; the witness cannot hear them. Yes, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The clip 45341A should be played from 00:55:35 to 00:56:55. And as I said, there is no spoken text. Mr. Davidovic, perhaps you could give us a comment on what we see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a review of a unit from Petrusic, previously in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure of the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is in front of the Municipal Assembly building, when the monument to King Peter was being unveiled, the liberator. I think it's Peter. I'm not sure. This is Mauzer holding the flag. This is General Simic. Prince Karadjordjevic. This is a Serbian deputy.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, do you know when and where this event happened?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in front of the Bijeljina Municipal Assembly building, when the monument was being unveiled. Actually, there was a monument here before, except that it had a five-pointed star on it. And instead of that, Petar Karadjordjevic, the liberator, was placed there. This was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to request the admission of this video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2856, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask for a clarification? It is stated here that this is a review of the unit Petrusic. Can the witness be asked to clarify which unit this is? What is this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you answer the question? The witness noted that he couldn't hear the names you referred to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not say Petrusic at any point. I said that this was a unit lined up in front of the sugar refinery. I don't know whose unit it is. But judging by the insignia on their shirts, on their blouses, on the camouflage uniforms, there is a black panther on it which I can assume would indicate that this is Arkan's Guard. I'm not sure, though, because I cannot see who the commander is. I wasn't able to see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to note that Mr. Karadzic will have a lot of time with the witness during cross-examination, and it's now the second time that he basically asks questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, that question was about to be asked by me because of the interpreter's notation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I also wonder -- your proposal to play the other two videos, nevertheless, is actually a good one, because the witness has reviewed the transcript, so he would know what is being said. So we can, indeed, play, if that is a convenient time, even without the words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let's do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And the first one would be 65 ter 45359A, and it is 00:34:30 to 00:36:26.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think we can actually stop it here.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, you have already mentioned that this is Arkan speaking. And did you have an opportunity to see this clip in your preparation for the testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And Arkan is referring here to an invitation of the TO Semberija and Bijeljina from the Crisis Staff to help the Serb people which were endangered here. Which crisis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff. Why don't we up-load the transcript in English and B/C/S, and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Because the witness had seen the video already, so we don't have to see the video, and we can work on the transcript, if you'd like to ask some questions. We switch to the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. That would, indeed, be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And we would just look at the first paragraph, where Arkan is stating that he came on the invitation of the TO Semberija and Bijeljina from the Crisis Staff to help the Serb people which were endangered. This Crisis Staff he's referring to, who would that be, Mr. Davidovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff which called Arkan to come to Bijeljina to liberate it, quote/unquote, they were members, first of all, of the Municipal Assembly, the president of the Municipal Assembly, the president of the Executive Board, the chief of the Defence, the chief of MUP, the head of the Economic Sector. These were members of the Crisis Staff. As needed later, the Crisis Staff expanded and invited other people from other organs or jurisdictions which at that point in time were important for them. Somebody from the Crisis Staff and the president of the SDS would be present in the area of the municipality where this would be happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when -- being, yourself, a citizen of Bijeljina, were the Serbs endangered in Bijeljina in April 1992, as Arkan says here?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not to that extent. [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I didn't hear what the witness said. There was no translation, at least not that I could hear.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I repeat?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We didn't hear after: "No, not to that extent."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the situation was not as serious that would require anybody from outside to intervene. I think that only an intervention by the police at the proper time would bring about a calming down of the situation. There was no need to resolve the situation with weapons, and there was no need for all the killings that happened at the time and after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I would like to have this admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have the indication of the time? Do you have that with you, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. It's 34:30 to 36:26. It's right in the beginning of this item.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2857, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to move on now to the video-clip 65 ter 45048, and that is the sequence from 00:01:00 to 00:04 -- oh, no, the other one. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: There is nothing said here, but, Mr. Davidovic, looking at this particular still, where is this parade or what I sort of call this, where is it taking place?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a review of Zeljko Raznatovic, Arkan's unit, in Bijeljina, in front of the Municipal Assembly building, and in the background you can see the monument that was erected. And we looked at that footage a little bit earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And do you know the flag that is being carried?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the flag of Arkan's guard, of his unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we move on a bit in this video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The person that you can see here at the front is Vojkan Djurkovic from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what role did -- I think you have described the role of Vojkan Djurkovic quite extensively in the statement, so we don't need to go into more details. Can we please move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop. [Interpretation] Stop. You can also see the unit that is on review, and you can see the area where the mosque used to be. It was demolished in 1983 [as interpreted], in the second half of 1983, and to the left is the youth hall. And if you play the video a little bit more, you would be able to see the court building.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, the transcript reflects that you said "in 1983." Is that a misspoken --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, 1993, 1993. The mosque was demolished in 1993, and I think this footage was recorded in 1994 because you can see the grass growing at the location where the mosque was, so sometime -- this is, then, some time later. This review was held in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can we just go on a bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop. [Interpretation] Stop. This is the court building. You can see it clearly now. This is between the court building and the youth hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can now go on playing it until we see a reward.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karadzic. The person is reporting or saluting. Arkan is standing next to him. I didn't see the person who saluted him and reported first.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Sir, the Battalion of the Serbian Volunteer Guard is lined up in your honour. Ranks ready for inspection for the guard and for you as the commander of the guard. Thank you very much. Mr. President, gratitude for you being there. This is not the end. This is the beginning. Thank you very much, Mr. President. Would you be so kind to say a few words? "I am deeply thankful and I congratulate you, and I hope that we will meet again in peace and you will always have a place in the heart of those you have defended. Thank you. "Mr. President, in the name of the Serbian Volunteer Guard, I wish to say two words to you, which is that we're ready, if you call us, and that we will be back to defend our ancient homeland, to defend our woman and children, to defend the Serbian territory and our Orthodox religion. Thank you, Mr. President."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can stop here.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, were you aware of this event in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of it, but I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to have this video admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Exhibit P2858.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, you mentioned the details of your activities to establish law and order in Zvornik, Bijeljina and Brcko in the summer of 1992. I would like to put to you now some lists -- payment lists related to groups that were paid, and the first one to show you is 65 ter 14641. And as it is coming up: It is a payment list for TO members in April 1992. Mr. Davidovic, while preparing for your testimony, did you review this document? And can we have the next page in the B/C/S, please. Did you review this list?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did, I looked at everything individually and the payrolls that were shown to me later, as such.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Davidovic, can you read the handwritten note on the top right in this first page?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Payment carried out following conclusions of interim government number ...," such and such.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were you aware that such an interim government existed in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that there was a crisis staff. They said they had a government of sorts, but I believed it was all the Crisis Staff. Later, I had the opportunity to see a document showing that they already had a government, a separate government, that they had suspended all the laws, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And do you know who was heading this interim government or the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Mr. -- I can't recall his name right now. I cannot remember his name. I know the name, but at the moment I really just can't --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, no problem. Can we please have page 6 in the English and page 5 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And we see here that the payment is approved by Stevo Radic. Do you know which body this gentleman represents?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I think that that was the president of the Municipal Assembly or of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can we have the next page, please, in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And there is reference to members of a unit from Loznica. Loznica, is this in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are members of the paramilitary formation, volunteers who had come and who were being paid by the Crisis Staff, from their fund.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And were you aware that there was a group from Loznica in Zvornik and the region at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrested the Yellow Wasps group then, I also arrested people from Loznica, Mali Zvornik, Sabac, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we have this document admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2859, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have 65 ter 00633 brought up on the screen, please. And as it is coming up: It is a pay list as well for the -- we have here a pay list, if you briefly look at this one. And can we also have the next page, please. Yes, yes. This list that you see -- can we just go back to the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: These people listed here, do you know them, some of them?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this Marko Pavlovic, who was chief of the TO -- actually, I think these were TO employees who received some compensation for something. I don't know what for, but I think that there is a reference to members of the TO Staff, the one that was headed by Marko Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we have this document admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2860, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would now like to have 65 ter 00673 be brought up on the screen, and it is another pay list.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, would you please read the handwritten words on the top right of the B/C/S version, what it says?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "The 2nd Tank Company."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you know that the Zvornik TO had a tank unit?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had a few tanks, and they were making some kind of armoured train, and this armour was supposed to protect it from bullets. And then with these two tanks and with this armoured train, they would go to liberate Kalesija, as they said, and then move further on to Tuzla, within the Territorial Defence -- or, rather, these paramilitary formations that were headed by the Yellow Wasps, and this Pavlovic, they actually had multiple rocket-launchers and other weapons. I think that, objectively speaking, the Territorial Defence does not have that kind of thing, and it should not.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2861, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we now have 65 ter 00671 be brought up on the screen. And it is -- it's actually two other pay lists.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, as it refers here to Commander Zuca, who would that be?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is actually the paramilitary unit of Dragan Vukovic, nicknamed Zuca. That's the Yellow Wasps; that's the criminal group that did some work for the TO Staff, and later when they became renegades, when they became a classical paramilitary formation, they did what they did, and then they had problems with it. But probably we will be dealing with that later. But these are Zuca's paramilitaries or the Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have the last page in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Looking at the handwritten note -- the last page in both languages, please. Mr. Davidovic, looking at the handwritten note that is on there, are you able to who is authorising the payment to this group? --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approved by the commander of the staff of the TO; that is, that man Pavlovic, the one that is mentioned as commander of the TO Staff. It's a false name. He is not the person that he was introducing himself to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can this please be admitted, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I didn't follow, Mr. Davidovic, when you referred to a false name. Could you explain to me that? What did you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This Pavlovic who was commander of the TO Staff, he came from Serbia and he introduced himself by the name of Pavlovic. Actually, he was not that Pavlovic. He used that name falsely. Allegedly, he said that the State Security Service had sent him. However, I never received any official confirmation from the State Security of Serbia. But he did come from Serbia. Later on, when we arrested him and when he was brought before a court of law, his true name was established, he said who he was. I was also a witness before the court in Belgrade when the Yellow Wasps were being tried, and he was one of those persons tried then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll admit this as Exhibit P2862.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we now have 65 ter 00682 on the screen. It's another pay list with reference to Zuco.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: On top -- Mr. Davidovic, on top of this list there is a -- there is an abbreviation. Can we have this -- the top -- the very top. Yes. This abbreviation, "PB-Grupa, Zuca," "1st PB," what does it stand for?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roman numeral I says that this is a separate or a special combat group, Zuco; that is, this elite group, Vojin Vuckovic's brother, Dusko, and Miroslav, they were basically the core of the command of the Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2863, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would like to have 65 ter 00683 be brought up on the screen, please. And it is another payment list, and it is, as it says here, to Pivarski's group of the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, do you know this Pivarski group?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This unit, Pivarski, actually, their commander was Stojan Pivarski. He was a member of the Army of Republika Srpska, I think, and as far as I knew, in the beginning. Later on, he withdrew from the front-line, and in town he joined the Yellow Wasps and he placed himself under the command of the Yellow Wasps. He was also arrested among the people I arrested when I arrested the Yellow Wasps, because he said that he was a member of the Yellow Wasps and that he was under their command.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2864, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The next item is 65 ter 00660, and if that could be brought up.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And as we can see here, there is reference to "Beli Orlovi" or "White Eagles." Mr. Davidovic, were you aware that White Eagles were also participating in that area?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and they came, among others, as volunteers. Allegedly, at first when they arrived, they were with Captain Dragan. Later on, they joined the Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can that be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2865, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would like to ask 65 ter 23167 be brought up on the screen, please. And as it is coming up: Your Honour, it is a certification in relation to a number of similar documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, while preparing for your testimony, did you review a number of very similar documents related to payments or support of certain military formations in the months April to June 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw a large group of these documents that you showed me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand the second part of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you repeat the second part of the sentence? The interpreter didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They paid these paramilitary formations, the TO Staff paid them; volunteers, as they called them.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And is that -- what we see here, is that when you reviewed these documents, and is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you make comments in relation to the lists that you saw, and are they reflected here?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, these are my comments in relation to the list that you showed me.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would request the admission of this certificate and also the documents listed in the certificate. It is much more efficient to do it this way. But if you prefer to have all the lists be brought up, we can, of course, do that. But it would be much more efficient to simply admit the document and the certificate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber would be assisted by hearing from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I was thinking about this, and it seems like this is essentially a Rule 92 ter statement with associated exhibits, although it's being presented as sort of an addendum to it. But it's the same. They could have actually put all this material in the text of a 92 ter statement and used all of them as associated exhibits. So with that perspective, we don't really object to them doing this.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I also say something in addition?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We, indeed, had first -- had thought about just merging it into the amended -- the amalgamated statement. But as we had produced it already to the Court and to the Defence, we thought this -- it would be better to do it this way and not add a block to the amalgamated statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the position taken by the Defence and that the nature of these documents are limited to a similar kind, we'll admit this. They will be given numbers in due course.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we admit in one go or do you like each document to be admitted separately?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would suggest that each document be admitted separately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And I just want to refer to one fact. The very last document is slightly different. It's not a pay list. It is, rather, a document from the interim government, referring to a particular unit. If you would rather have this separate, then I can, of course, do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then why don't you deal with that document, and we'll admit the remaining --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All the documents. That will be done by the Court Deputy in due course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we then have 65 ter 00685 be brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And is that also one of the documents, Mr. Davidovic, that you looked at?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It is a permission by the head of the interim government, Branko Grujic. Does this name ring a bell with you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I couldn't remember a moment ago. Later on, I remembered. I wanted to tell you at the very end. He was actually president of the Crisis Staff. It says "Provisional Government" here. This shows unequivocally that they secured funds for the purchase of material for the manufacturing of uniforms that they were supposed to give to those units.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And Igor Markovic Special Unit, do you know what unit that is?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is someone who got killed at the end of the war. They immediately named the unit Igor Markovic in the beginning, but later on they grew into the Yellow Wasps and this name, Igor Markovic, was never mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2867, Exhibit P2866 being the certificates, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour -- no, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, in your statement you referred to an individual with the name of Branislav Filipovic, and his association with Mirko Blagojevic. And, Your Honour, just for reference, this is in paragraph 118. In this context, I would like to have 65 ter 06926 be brought up on the screen. And, Your Honour, you will see we have now a few documents that are in a bit of a bad quality, at least in relation to the B/C/S version. Mr. Davidovic, what do we have here?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a pass issued in the name of Branislav Filipovic, allowing him to leave the battle zone and Brcko municipality. It says that he is a volunteer. Otherwise, he was a member of the Radical Party, Mirko Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can you see who is issuing this pass?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the War Presidency, that's what it says here, the municipality, but I cannot see who signed it. It's illegible.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And for what purposes were such documents needed and issued?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because at the entry points into Brcko and Bijeljina, and all along the road between Brcko and Bijeljina, there were check-points manned by police, paramilitaries, or the military; it doesn't matter. You were supposed to show an ID and a pass showing that you were allowed to be on the road on some mission.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can this please be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Does Mirko Blagojevic's name appear on this pass? You mentioned his name in your answer. Do you understand my question? Mr. Davidovic, you said: "Otherwise, he was a member of the Radical Party, Mirko Blagojevic." Did you mean Mirko Blagojevic was the president of the Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mirko Blagojevic was president of the Radical Party in Bijeljina; that is to say, the Bijeljina Radical Party had its own unit, and Branislav Filipovic, among others, belonged to that unit at the start of the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2874, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have 65 ter 06970 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, what are we seeing here?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff is providing a certificate to Branislav Filipovic, allowing him to move freely, without any limitation. And this guarantee is provided by the Semberija and Majevica SAO Crisis Staff. Mirjana Simic travels with this person, his common-law wife, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And for which Crisis Staff is Mr. Savic signing this?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on behalf of the Crisis Staff of Majevica and Semberija; or rather, the SAO of Majevica and Semberija.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we have the next page in the B/C/S. There is only a small note there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, who is signing this, the back side, and on -- and what stamp does it show, what reference is made?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was signed by some person named Dobrica Peric for Petar Bacic. Petar Bacic was a reserve policeman. He was an active-duty policeman. Then he retired, and then he was activated again in order to have the check-points manned. And down there you see a stamp of Republika Srpska, or, rather, the SDS, the Serb Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2875, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we now have 65 ter 07848 be brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It is very hard to read, but can you tell us what we are looking at?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a receipt that was received by the Military Command, I think, of the town of Belgrade, the command of the defence of the city of Belgrade. I think, 132/2, the 20th of June, and then various types of ammunition are referred to here further down; mortars, Zoljas, Osas, and other types of weapons. Actually, this is just ammunition that was given to them. I don't know who, it just says "FI." I don't see exactly who this was given to. However, this receipt was issued by the Command of the Military District from Belgrade for a certain type of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can this be admitted, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2876, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so that you can see, in the --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just ask something? Do we have in Serbian the same thing that we have in the translation? I did not see "Brcko" anywhere, and I don't understand whether this is a translation of this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to also mention that in the English translation, we can read a lot more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And I have tried to get a better copy, but obviously it was not possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we collapse the English and zoom in on the B/C/S a bit further?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's give it a try. Upper part. We can zoom in a bit further. Could you read the handwritten parts there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says "5" or "S," but I think it is "OSS-10," and then "MOK Srbije, and then in parenthesis "TO," and I can't see the rest. And then down here, it says, "KODB." I assume that it's the command of the district either of the city of Belgrade or of State Security. I cannot read it. The number is "3-132/2 of the 20th of June," and I cannot see anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: If we go to the very end of this document, Your Honour. Zoom in on the -- below this, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you make out who receives it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Fil," and then "VIC," and the signature is illegible. The stamp is of the Military Post of Belgrade. And "Miroslav Radic --" no, "Radisavljevic" [phoen], something like that. I'm not sure. I just know the first three letters are "Rad," "Radi," and I cannot read the rest.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do we link this up to Brcko?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: At least according to the English translation, there seems to have been a better version at some point in time where you could read. If you could go to the very top -- the very top again.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can see there is, in brackets, a "TO," and then we can't read the rest. I would assume that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But where do the interpreters get "Brcko"? So your assumption is there must be a better version of it?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I tried to get a better version. I even asked whether we could have the original here in the courtroom, but it didn't work out; at least not for now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. On the back of this same receipt, there is this text. And if you could turn the back of this document, this very same document, we can have a look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is only --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: There is nothing on the back. We can try to bring the original in here and come back to it later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay, very well. I note the time. Let's think about it during the break. We'll have a break for half an hour. We'll resume at five past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, we do have now the original in the courtroom, and can this be -- please be put on the ELMO. Can we have it with -- yes, yes, this first list part.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, can you now see who is receiving this, or do you now see the right-hand side reference?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's supposed to be received by the Territorial Defence of Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can we please move down to the end so that we can see the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you now see who is receiving this to hand it over?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branislav -- B. Filipovic took it, personally. I can add one thing. Branislav Filipovic was in the theatre of Brdjani in the end, and he was killed after. He never got to another theatre of war. That's how I know it's all about Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Your Honour, can this now be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It has already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please think about up-loading a B/C/S version of better quality.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We could scan it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It has been done; okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we now please have 65 ter 07169 be brought up on the screen. Yes. Can we zoom in a bit more in the B/C/S version so it's easier to read.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, what are we looking at?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a paper giving Branislav Filipovic - his ID number is not clearly seen - approval to bring ammunition to Brcko for the anti-tank gun. The calibre is indicated - hand held rocket-launchers, Zolja, Osa, and hand-grenades. Lieutenant Predrag Manojlovic's signature is there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have the B/C/S version, the second page.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: There is a reference, Mr. Davidovic, to a Mitar Bolero. Can you tell us who that is?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a telephone number, and it says "Mitar Bolero." That's a person from Brcko, where the Radical Party headquarters were, headed by Vojvoda Blagojevic. And this man, Bolero, was a member of the Radical Party, and his own house was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we -- could we get the date of this document? It is important.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is no date on it, but perhaps Mr. Davidovic can help us.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You said that Mr. Filipovic was killed. Do you know when he -- approximately when he was killed?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think sometime in July or August. More likely in August 1992, or perhaps earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, it wasn't August; it was earlier. It could even been the end of May or June, because I was in Sarajevo when I heard of the death of Brano Filipovic in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What the Defence is interested in is whether this was a JNA garrison or the VRS garrison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's a subject you can explore in your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2877, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we now please have 65 ter 13255 be brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And as it is coming up: Mr. Davidovic, you have mentioned Mirko Blagojevic a couple of times, and you also referred to him in your statement, where you mentioned that he, in fact, at some point in time protected Muslims in Bijeljina. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko Blagojevic was president of the Serbian Radical Party in Bijeljina. I'm talking exclusively about Bijeljina in the period I know about. Mirko Blagojevic was a very positive character during the war, in terms of protecting the Muslims, their lives and protecting their lives. Mirko Blagojevic was emphatic in opposing the decisions of the Crisis Staff and the SDS to move the Muslims out, to expel them or kill them. He fought this by public statements, public appearances and speeches, all of which encouraged the Muslims and gave them some trust in him as their defender. Whoever would like to say any different, this simply is a fact. That's what happened in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Looking at this document here, it is an announcement of Blagojevic related to the murder of the Sarajlic and Sejmenovic families. Are you aware of this declaration and his request for an investigation?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that public announcement, because it was the only one about the killing of two families. When those families were taken to the Drina River and liquidated, the local authorities tried to cover that up. They didn't want it to go into the public or anyone to know about it. There was a decision of the Presidency at the time to prohibit any public statements by political parties in the media, so Mirko Blagojevic used a ruse and he wrote this public statement as the commander of Serbian Chetniks, making it sound like it was coming from a military unit. And the radio editor, Pero Simic, decided to release this, and, indeed, it was broadcast on the radio that these two families, Sejmenovic and Sarajlic, were killed by the Drina River, and there was a whole story about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, Mr. Blagojevic blames the murders on the RS MUP Special Unit. Do you know or did you come across information who murdered these families?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my earlier testimony in the Krajisnik case and the Mico Stanisic case, I said, more than once, that members of the police, headed by Dusko Malovic, a special police unit, in the sole jurisdiction of Mico Stanisic, the interior minister, were brought to Bijeljina and installed there. And Dusko Malovic told me personally, a month later when I returned from Pljevlja, where I was with my unit, that what had been done had been done on the orders of the Crisis Staff and the chief of Public Security in Bijeljina, and this operation was meant to further intimidate the Muslim population so that they leave Republika Srpska and Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when you say after you returned from this Pljevlja, when was this, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been the end of July or early August when those killings occurred. I don't know the exact dates, but that's the period, in July or August.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No. I was asking about your conversation with Mr. Malovic.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could have been in September or October that year, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would request the admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2878, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would ask that Exhibit 65 ter 18846 be brought up. However, before that is done: We have a public redacted version and an unredacted version. And before we do this, can we go briefly into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, under paragraph 2 in both languages, and continuing, actually, if we now also go to the page 2 in both languages, there is quite a detailed description of personalities and their actions; in particular, their crimes. Did you have time to review this?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what is mentioned here, is it an accurate description of the events at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the situation which is reported.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And there is -- in the middle of the page in both languages, there is a reference to Colonel Nikola Dencic and his co-operation with Zuco. Do you know who this officer is and whether he co-operated, indeed, with Zuco?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nikola Dencic was the corps commander. He was colonel quarter-master. He was, as I said, the corps commander, and he had a security officer, Dusan Atanackovic. They were very closely tied to the Yellow Wasps, because I know that during the war they used to come to Ugljevik, and at the prison there, a make-shift prison in a boiler room in Ugljevik, Zuco and his brother, Repic, used to come and beat the prisoners. And this make-shift prison held mostly Croats and Muslims who had been detained at check-points between Bijeljina and Tuzla, and every non-Serb would be stopped and, without any reason whatsoever, taken to that prison. And I know that he did that together with this security chief. I know people -- other people came in to beat the prisoners, and mistreat them, and make them sing Chetnik songs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just be of assistance? The Chamber cannot see the threat that was made. It was redacted by mistake. It should be seen in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we have the next page, please, in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And there is a reference to a visit of Karadzic and Mladic on the 30th of June -- the 30th of June, it says, 30th of June. And a discussion is mentioned about the training centre in Divic. Mr. Davidovic, are you aware of the training centre in Divic, and do you know anything about a concern about this training centre that Mladic or Karadzic had?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think this should be allowed. It doesn't follow from the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In the document, there is, indeed, a reference to the training centre, Captain Dragan's volunteer training centre. And then as we follow through, General Mladic is making comments related to it. And I'm just asking the witness whether he knows anything about this training centre and concerns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. What is your concern, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's leading. Which was done by Karadzic and Mladic, this does not follow from the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I see a reference to General Mladic and you in the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the translation which had -- by Karadzic and Mladic. This is a leading question which does not follow from the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I see a passage -- yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think the way the question was phrased, a training centre that Karadzic or Mladic had, may have given the wrong impression that they were the operators of the training session, as opposed to the concern that they had about the training centre, because I, myself, when I first heard the question, thought it was implying that Dr. Karadzic and General Mladic had some training session -- or centre. But it appears that the question was intended to address the concern that they had about training centres, so I think that may be the cause of the confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Robinson. On that basis, we can proceed. Yes, Mr. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, do you know about this training centre and that there were concerns about it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware that there were -- and I will be free enough to say there were several training centres in Divic, and paramilitary formations gathered there. Divic was a location which was like a dead-end in Republika Srpska. You could not enter it from any side by the Muslim forces, because it's in the Drina area between Serbia and Bosnia. At the beginning of the war, a training centre was formed in Divic, led by Captain Dragan, who was sent from Serbia, with the aim of training volunteers. And then they were sent from military units, and younger, more fit and capable people were sent to be trained at the camp by Captain Dragan. I know a person who went to a training course, and then later he was returned as not being fit enough to go and complete the whole training. Later, people were sent there. Also Vuckovic, he spent some time in Divic. And then later, when the Yellow Wasps came, there was a special unit there of the Republican MUP, led by Karisik, who also spent some time in Divic. So Divic is referred to in all these military reports and information. I know General Mladic was against paramilitary formations. I don't know whether he went there or not, and I don't know if this has anything to do with Mr. Karadzic, whether they went there together to visit it. That's something that I really cannot help you with. This was a period when all kinds of things were being said. They were there perhaps to improve the rating of the centre, itself. But I don't know, really, if they were actually there or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you. Can we please have the next page and in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: There is, in the beginning -- in the first paragraph, there is a reference to a man with the nickname Crni, and that -- the problems with him. Do you know this person and what the problems were?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A person with the nickname Crni came from Serbia, and he was in a part of the unit that was stationed in Bosanski Samac. This group, among others, came to Bijeljina as well. At one time, I think they also attempted or actually carried out a rape. As far as I know, some 10 or 20 days ago, the Special Prosecutor's Office from Belgrade initiated proceedings against some persons, even for one person with the name Crni. I assume that is that group of persons that actually carried out a lot of crimes, mistreatments, killings. They harassed and abused some women. They committed crimes in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can this document be admitted, one the full version under seal, and the other one --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. We don't have an objection to this, but I just want to note that it's on an exceptional basis because it could be said this constitutes the statement of a third person and might not otherwise be admissible. Most of this is a report of an interview with an individual, but in this particular case we don't object because we feel it's more advantageous to us than detrimental.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll deal with it when the issues arise. We'll admit this. We'll give separate numbers for both versions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibits P2879, under seal, and Exhibit P2880, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we just establish that the threat there was to kill? In the English version, this is redacted, but in the B/C/S version --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, because we have both versions, we can compare that later on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it's been redacted in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have an unredacted version in our exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now have document D00450 brought up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, it is a note by the RS MUP to several CSBs, inter alia, Bijeljina, of the 19th of July, 1992. Did you have an opportunity to review this document?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had the opportunity to look at the document when I was preparing for my testimony with the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in the beginning, there is a reference made to a meeting of MUP executives in Belgrade on the 11th of July, 1992, relating to problems with paramilitary units; in particular, their crimes. Do you know about this meeting and who attended?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was a MUP meeting that was held. It was a meeting in Bosanska Villa, attended by the minister, his deputies, his assistants, and the chiefs of the CSBs and of the administrations, certain administrations within the ministry. It's a little bit unusual to have a ministerial -- ministry meeting in a different state, in Belgrade, but this is possible too.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the problems referred to in this document, are they consistent with what you, yourself, were aware of and saw on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What I was saying is accepted. Actually, it's been confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can we have a look at paragraph G. That's the next page, I would think. And in the English, it is D, paragraph D. In the B/C/S, it's G.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: If you look at what is described here, a reference to the treatment and custody of prisoners, and the reference to collection camps into which the army brings Muslim residents, do you know about such collection centres, as they are called here, and treatment of prisoners in detention facilities?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war, the crisis staffs adopted a decision to exert pressure on the Muslim population, in the sense of their mobilisation and engaging militarily in the Serbian Army ranks. And then there was a series of questions put with some people who were opposed to this. And then as far as I know, within the army's jurisdiction a decision was made to form collection centres, or, as they called them in the beginning, labour camps, where certain Muslim persons would be placed. At the time, I asked Colonel Ilic, the colonel of the corps who came after Dencic, what was the meaning -- why these camps were being formed, on what grounds, what would they be used for. And he said pursuant to the model during World War II, when the Americans also placed all the Germans who were in Germany to some collection camps so that they would not be used by their enemies, that was the reason why they were doing that too, these people were being placed into these military camps, certain persons. However, later the camps, as they called them, collection centres or labour camps, turned into something else. Citizens were being brought here, mostly of Muslim ethnicity from Brcko, Zvornik, Bijeljina, all the other places in Central Bosnia, and in the beginning these people were taken for work duties. But later, when the International Red Cross arrived, they did not release them. They were registered. This was already in late 1992/early 1993, and they could not manipulate to the extent that they could at the beginning. As for MUP and this document, what they meant by handing over these camps to MUP organs of Republika Srpska, that is not clear to me. What does MUP have to do with these camps, and why would they be handed over, even though I know that when we're talking about the Yellow Wasps in Zvornik, Celopek, they were holding Muslims in the Dom who were brought from Muslim settlements, especially from Kozluk. They were placed there. At that time, the "milicija" was providing security and guarding them. There was no "policija" at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, this is already in evidence so there is nothing to be done here. I would like to call up now P1500. The document is also already in evidence. And as it is coming up: It's an order from Ratko Mladic, dated the 28th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
