So a fine was imposed, as if I had committed a traffic violation. So, all right, I agree it was a criminal case, but, nevertheless, it was only a fine that was imposed. Is there anything that is in dispute there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Nothing, thank you. And then the company called Meteor, was it -- actually, can this be marked for identification, this second-instance judgement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1404, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3641.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the company Meteor bring charges against you and your company that you are also general manager of?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you charged with avoiding to pay your debts?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was acquitted on first instance, and you don't have that judgement. As for the second-instance judgement, when I returned, the second-instance judgement said that I was supposed to pay about 246.000 marks to Meteor. I appealed to the Supreme Court of the BH, or, rather, Republika Srpska, and the Supreme Court of Republika Srpska annulled that decision of the second-instance court. Again, on a second time, the District Court found in favour of the company called Meteor. However, as they were resolving the case the second time, the Supreme Court passed the same kind of judgement; namely, the final judgement of the first-instance Court was confirmed, and it states that the District Court judgement was not lawful. I have the rulings of all three Courts, and I can show them to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said after you returned. Returned from where?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the 1st of March, 2004, the 1st of March, 2004, and you were in The Hague in June 2005.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, you are trying -- well, the proceedings took place even before they were before the Court. When I received the first-instance judgement, there were no difficulties because the Court found in my favour. However, the proceedings went on, and the second-instance Court ruled against me. The Supreme Court annulled the decision of the District Court and returned the case to the District Court. The District Court confirmed its own second-instance judgement, the one that you say you have -- actually, the one that is here before us now, and then, yet again, I appealed to the Supreme Court. And you have to wait for two years, and even more. And then perhaps a year and a half earlier on, the Supreme Court supported the judgement of the Lower Court in Bijeljina. And I will tell you why the District Court is passing such judgements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, but that is not our subject now. The subject of what I'm saying now is that all of this happened before your testimony here.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of this was happening during the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you testified here in June 2005; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, but the proceedings went on until 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then I get a final decision acquitting me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be marked for identification as Exhibit D1405.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you also sued by a company called Zitopromet? Did they sue the company of which you are the owner and director?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D3652. 1D3652.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this a case where the judge is Halida Buljugic, and the case is between two companies over a debt of 11.250 convertible marks, and did the judge decide that you have to pay that debt?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not really see the relevance. This is a businessman who has, of course, in the run of his business, disputes with his customers or his co-operating companies. I don't really see how this could reflect on the credibility of this witness. That is usual for everyone who runs a business.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very much so. Mr. Karadzic, do you have an explanation as to the relevance of this document, having heard Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff's statement?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you wait to see the next document, you will see that there is continuity, a pattern of not paying debts, committing fraud, forcible entry into apartments, abuse of authority and position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll consider admitting this document later on. Proceed. Yes, Mr. Davidovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said even this judgement was quashed and I was acquitted by the District Court in Bijeljina. I don't know if Mr. Karadzic has that judgement. If he doesn't, I do. And if I may clear one thing up. It refers to business fraud. I was a witness there. I interceded with the director of that company that flour be issued to a certain man. It's a company called Meteor. People issue flour, and they write on the receipt: "At the intervention of Mico Davidovic." You can see from those papers that I did not take that flour, my name was not on the dispatch documents. I was later acquitted, but I was acquitted because I just went there and paid for it. I met that man, the director, two years later, and he told me, Do you know the man who received the flour never paid for it? I said, What do you mean? I'm very embarrassed that I was the one who interceded to get him that flour, so I went to that business and paid the debt, the debt of another person before that company. And in the meantime, proceedings were already underway against me, but the Appeals Court acquitted me. And the whole thing repeats itself many times; proceedings, acquittal, proceedings, acquittal. And Mr. Karadzic is trying to consistently portray me as a fraud and a criminal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you sued or charged with fraud other times?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I was involved in three cases, and all the three judgements are acquittals. And at this moment, there are no proceedings against me. All the judgements against me are acquittals, and they are final judgements, and I can provide them to be included in the evidence if it is of any interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But each of these cases were before you testified in Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only started before, but they lasted a long time and went from lower courts to higher courts to appeal courts, et cetera. And many years later, I would always be acquitted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 1D3642.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this a criminal report by Jelenko Knezevic, charges of fraud? He was suing you for defrauding him -- or, rather, defaulting on your obligations under a contract; is it right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I was acquitted by both the Appeals Court and the District Court in both proceedings.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I see no value and relevance in this document. Everybody can make a criminal complaint. The result of the investigation and the result of the prosecution, if there is one, that's -- that would be relevant, but not someone making a complaint because they have a disagreement on a business contract.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. If I could just be heard very briefly. I think in common-law systems, where we have jury trials, there are strict rules about admissibility of such things, and it probably would not be admissible. But in this Tribunal, where we have professional Judges and items are weighed, as opposed to excluded, I think this is a circumstances under which a document like this, which does go to his credibility, given the limitations expressed by Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, it still ought to be admitted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, they're pretty severe limitations, aren't they, Mr. Robinson? It's an allegation; no more.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And I think with that weight, it should be admitted, because there's not the danger of your being unable to fairly assess that, whereas in a jury trial, there might be such a danger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: The only problem is that, as you know, Mr. Robinson, there are a myriad of documents that the Trial Chamber is going to have to look at in due course, and it may be that this falls into the category of a document that the defendant would agree is not, of itself, of any real moment. But that's just an observation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The other members of the Chamber agree with Judge Morrison's view. This will not be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see one more document before we finish, 3640.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, did you run into trouble with the law even when you were young?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you're asking me the same things Mr. Krajisnik asked me. As a minor, when I was 15 years old, with boys of the same age, I was involved in a fight, and I was treated by the law as a minor. Does it please you that I have a juvenile criminal record as a minor? But that didn't stop me from finishing university, getting employed with the police and working. You are now bringing it up, just like Mr. Krajisnik did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were 16 or 17?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe 16 or 17. I was a minor, in any case.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the previous case, Mr. Krajisnik, indeed, wanted to have this document be admitted. It wasn't admitted. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think that's --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The fact that I did not object using this is actually the witness, himself, said that he would like to be able to answer those kind of things. Therefore, under this limited -- under this point, I have no objection, but want to make, again, clear that there is no real value in this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I respond? It would be a brief response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is a criminal record that is related to an event when he was 16 years old. And given that he admitted what is contained in this document, the Chamber does not see any need to admit this. So we'll not admit this. Given the time, we'll adjourn for to-day and resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Although the ruling has been made, I just want to say why I offered this. This would shed light on the conduct of this witness in his later years as the basis of a pattern of aggressive behaviour. That was the reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's an unnecessary comment on your part, Mr. Karadzic. Tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 29th day of June, 2011, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
